correctness.rationale: On an oriented path the homogeneous vertex equations give the repeated values a,s_i,a+s_i in characteristic two. When t_0=0, substituting the forced s_i into the terminal equations gives (1+t_2)a=(1+t_2)b=0, with t_2 and t_1 of the same parity. Otherwise a=b, and with S the sum of the free first internal values, the two constraints are (1+t_1)a+S=0 and (1+t_0+t_1)a+S=0. Since t_0>0, the constraint on S has rank one; the difference t_0 a=0 gives the other bit of rank exactly when t_0 is odd. These reductions are necessary and sufficient even for length two and when r=2. Eulerian degree parity gives (I+A)1=1, so all-on solutions are the translate of the kernel with size 2^nullity.
residual_risks: The matrix census is finite; the terminal-equation proof establishes the universal classification.

evidence: Edwards uses length n_i equal to the number of internal vertices, not the edge length ell_i. Its reduced counts t and m therefore equal the frozen t_0 and t_2, respectively, with l=r. The paper permits general moduli and some multigraph reductions.

Corollary 2.8 gives an iff for winnability under a surjective linear map from the old coloring variables to the reduced colors (set the removed coordinates to zero to obtain any target). Section 4 applies the reduction along theta paths, so codimension is preserved.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Reduction to a smaller theta graph loses no codimension. The two-path case is a cycle, with the classical period-three nullity rule also obtained by closing the same two-dimensional recurrence around the cycle.

evidence: For t=0 the two-terminal matrix has off-diagonal l-2m=0 mod 2 and diagonal 1-m. Its image codimension is 0 for m even and 2 for m odd; m=t_2 and t_1 have the same parity here.

For t>0 the theorem equates all t differences b_i,2-b_i,1, giving t-1 independent constraints. The divisibility by gcd(2-6m-3t+2l,2) contributes nothing when t is odd and one further linear constraint when t is even. It is independent because the terminal color b_0 appears with coefficient 1 while it occurs in none of the difference constraints.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These dimensions are exactly the frozen four cases. Every solvable right-hand side then has 2^nullity preimages, and with even degrees the all-on right-hand side is solvable. No additional singular-case theorem is needed.

evidence: Edwards et al. classify precisely which right-hand sides belong to the image of the closed-neighborhood matrix after reduction. Over F_2, rank-nullity identifies codimension of that image with the number of binary degrees of freedom in a solvable press system.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A condition for each coloring is stronger than an invertibility test and must not be compared only with the uniqueness corollary.

evidence: The Resultary matches involve forest convolution on theta graphs or all-on strategy weight on GP(n,3), not the same table of binary vertex-matrix nullities. Dolati–Golalizadeh's symbolic matching formula is for the same theta graph but gives total matchings; its parity, with Codsi et al., gives the zero-nullity cases only.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: An exact invariant table for a different operator or counting problem does not establish all kernel dimensions. The decisive prior coverage instead comes from the winnability equations.

originality.rationale: The full nullity law, not just uniqueness, is a direct characteristic-two codimension reading of Edwards et al. (2010), Corollary 2.8 and Theorem 4.3 on winnable colorings of generalized theta graphs. For a square matrix the codimension of the winnable-color space is the nullity. That equivalence supplies the positive-nullity cases even though the earlier paper emphasizes winnability rather than the count of press subsets.
residual_risks: This is verified coverage of the mathematics, not attribution of historical priority among earlier papers. No priority claim depends on a catalogue date.
